title: One Open Call per Unit and the Shared Diagnostic Fee, Repair and Emergency Service Calls
content:
## Standard

1. A unit may have only one call in booked or dispatched status at a time under Repair and Emergency Service Calls. A new problem on a unit that already has an open call is added to that call; it is not booked again.
2. When two or more units at the same home are looked at on the same visit, they share one call's diagnostic fee wherever the call class charges no second diagnostic fee for a second unit. Every call class does so. The second unit is diagnosed on the open call, and no second diagnostic fee or premium is charged.
3. Calls on different units booked for different days are separate visits, each with its own fees.

## Evidence

Whether a unit already has an open call is read from the company's call records, never from the caller's account. The record checked is the unit's existing calls and their status. Only a call for the same unit in booked or dispatched status is the same object. A completed, closed or cancelled call on the unit does not count as open, and an open call on a different unit does not count either.

## Cases (hypothetical)

| Records show | Request | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Furnace has a call in booked status | New noise reported on the same furnace | Added to the booked call, no second booking |
| Furnace call is dispatched; technician on site | Customer asks the technician to look at the air conditioner too | Air conditioner diagnosed on the open call; no second diagnostic fee or premium |
| Furnace call completed last week | New problem on the furnace | The earlier call is no longer open; a new call may be booked |
| Air conditioner call on Monday, furnace call on Thursday | Both kept | Two separate visits, each with its own fees |
